selected.title: Government offers small businesses a trust tax workaround
selected.summary: Those with discretionary trusts can be exempt from the new minimum 30 per cent tax if they agree to hold their trust distributions constant.
selected.why: New tax policy exemption mechanism for small business discretionary trusts.
selected.fullText: Government offers small businesses a trust tax workaround - ABC News Skip to main content Skip to news navigation, settings and search Explore the ABC news iview listen Loading ABC News News Home Government offers small businesses a trust tax workaround Share Share article Government offers small businesses a trust tax workaround By economics reporter Tom Crowley Topic: Federal Government Posted Thu 3 Sep 2026 at 2:02pm Thu 3 Sep 2026 at 2:02pm Thu 3 Sep 2026 at 2:02pm , updated Thu 3 Sep 2026 at 4:07pm Thu 3 Sep 2026 at 4:07pm Thu 3 Sep 2026 at 4:07pm Treasurer Jim Chalmers has proposed a workaround to the minimum discretionary trust tax. ( ABC News: Ian Cutmore ) In short: The federal government has proposed a workaround for small businesses who were worried about paying state stamp duties when they restructure out of discretionary trusts to avoid the proposed minimum tax. They will instead be able to restructure their affairs without actually changing their trust structures, remaining exempt from the tax as long as they do not vary their distributions. What's next? The draft legislation is open for consultation for two weeks. abc.net.au/news/government-offers-small-businesses-a-trust-tax-workaround/107112000 Link copied Share Share article Small businesses could avoid being stung by stamp duty when they restructure to escape Labor's minimum tax on discretionary trusts, under a workaround proposed by Treasurer Jim Chalmers. Draft laws to enact the 30 per cent trust tax were released for feedback on Thursday. The tax is the last of the major tax changes from the May federal budget to be legislated. Fears about stamp duty had been raised with the government during consultation, with small business lobby COSBOA warning those who used discretionary trusts could be left with "an impossible choice between a higher tax burden or a costly restructure". The workaround would allow trustees to avoid an official restructure, exempting them from the tax if they agreed to shift their existing beneficiaries to a fixed-income structure. Why stamp duty loomed as an issue Stamp duties are collected by states and territories when property is transferred or transacted. Financial assets count as property, so small business restructures usually trigger stamp duty. Trust tax relief hinges on stamp duty Small businesses affected by the change are in limbo as states decide whether to waive stamp duty fees. reason: Tax policy creates perverse incentive: allowing businesses to avoid restructuring costs by locking in distributions may entrench inefficient trust structures and reduce capital mobility.
angle: The stamp duty workaround solves the wrong problem by subsidizing structural rigidity rather than addressing whether the 30% discretionary trust tax itself is sound policy.
